* EKC hypothesis: early studies posit an inverted-U relation between CO2 intensity and per-capita income.
- Cross-country panels show peaking emissions at high income; transitions depend on energy mix, trade openness, institutions.
* Decomposition literature attributes emission changes to growth, structural shifts, energy efficiency, technology.
- Results vary by region; developing economies often show rising CO2 due to industrialization.
* Econometric research uses panel cointegration, granger causality, nonlinear threshold models.
- Evidence includes bidirectional growth-emission links, asymmetric effects, threshold income levels.
* Policy studies examine carbon taxes, emission trading, green R&D, renewable subsidies.
- Findings suggest emission reductions can coexist with modest growth costs; revenue recycling strengthens outcomes.
